states.note: Unanimous; the first state to ratify.
The convention's minority published its "Address and Reasons of Dissent" days later.
Ratified with recommended amendments, a pattern later states followed.
The ninth state, so the Constitution would take effect among the ratifying states. Its convention had adjourned once, in February, without voting.
After Patrick Henry and George Mason led the opposition; recommended a bill of rights and other amendments.
Ratified with recommended amendments and a circular letter calling for a second convention.
Its first convention, at Hillsborough in summer 1788, voted 184 to 84 neither to ratify nor to reject. It ratified at Fayetteville after Congress had sent amendments to the states.

Never sent delegates to the Convention. In a referendum on March 24, 1788, which most Federalists boycotted, voters rejected the Constitution 2,714 to 238 (one count; tallies differ slightly). A convention finally ratified by two votes.
